slides.title: Where we are
items: Your servo is wired on the regulator board's 5 V and follows the potentiometer on A0, with your completed Day15_servo_template.c on the Nucleo.

The reading introduced the photocell, a resistor whose resistance drops as more light falls on it, along with a family of sensors that work the same way. The reading furthermore reviewed the voltage divider that turns a resistance into a voltage for the ADC, introduced the photocell's datasheet, and explained what a solar tracker is.

Today we'll put the photocell into a voltage divider, work through Part 1 of Lab 8, add the photocells to the tracker arm of your servo, and discuss how the tracker's feedback loop can be implemented.

What you need today: Nucleo and breadboard, the servo on its stand with the tracker arm, the regulator board and its adapter, your two photocells and two 10 kΩ resistors, the alligator-to-breadboard clips, your multimeter, the AD2, and a flashlight (the one on your phone will work).
